clue.text: Bread said to be for Pat

indicators.note: said to be signals that the word heard aloud gives the answer's sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the word that comes before pat in pitter-pat, the patter of tiny feet

explanation.surface: Someone claims a loaf has been set aside for a person called Pat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a person's name, but it is the second half of pitter-pat; the word that goes before it, PITTER, sounds like the flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow Middle Eastern bread, so it is an example of bread.

clue.text: Reciprocally, race home after river races for another option …

indicators.note: after places home's letters following river's in the build

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
IN means at home
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

indicators.note: another version of the word option is a reshuffle of its letters

explanation.surface: Thinking of horses racing home after splashing through a river, someone weighs up another choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reciprocally' opens the run of linked clues whose answers are all 'X to X' phrases; the anagram of OPTION, prompted by 'another', supplies OPOINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is a cross-country steeplechase for amateur riders, so it is a kind of horse race.

clue.text: … and, talking of other countries, New Year to absorb summer

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival
to eat is to absorb or take in
ete is French for summer, fitting a clue about foreign tongues

explanation.surface: Continuing a list, someone discussing foreign lands mentions a New Year festival swallowing up the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues the linked 'X to X' theme from 1 down; the definition is that theme put into a foreign tongue, the French version of head to head.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally head to head in French, a private conversation between two is the foreign-language member of this reciprocal family.

clue.text: Range of maps

definitions.meaning: the ... mountains are a range in north-west Africa
a bound collection of maps is a book of this name

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a North African mountain range and a bound volume of maps.

clue.text: Mistake about uneven movement characteristic of old soldier

indicators.note: about means the word for mistake goes round the uneven movement

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder
to limp is to walk unevenly, so a limp is an uneven movement

explanation.surface: A blunder over someone's halting gait is typical of an elderly army veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a pompous, reactionary cartoon officer in 1930s British newspapers, hence the adjective for stuffy old-soldier attitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous and reactionary like the cartoon Colonel Blimp describes the stereotype of a crusty retired officer.

clue.text: I was first to say, in case of low standard, this is destined for the cup

definitions.text: this is destined for the cup

indicators.note: in case of puts the other letters inside the word for low standard, as its case

parts.note: bog-standard means ordinary or of low standard, so bog stands for it
to have led is to have been first
EG, for example, is the usual abbreviation for say

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they spoke up first when standards slipped, and the item is bound for a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cup' is not a trophy but an egg cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg is served sitting in an egg cup, so it is the thing meant for the cup.

clue.text: Particular couple

definitions.meaning: a particular is a single detail or article
a romantically linked couple is called an ...

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a separate detail on a list and a pair seen as a couple.

clue.text: Fisherman leader in this town?

parts.note: Saint Peter was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A riddle asks whether the chief fisherman lives in this particular town.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterhead is a major fishing port in north-east Scotland, so a leading fisherman would plausibly be found there.
explanation.definitionFit: This Aberdeenshire town is one of Britain's largest fishing ports, the natural home of a leading fisherman.

clue.text: Southern Englishman, say, is like a slug

indicators.note: say signals that the word for Englishman is used for its sound

parts.note: limey is American slang for an Englishman

explanation.surface: Someone from the south of England is compared to a garden pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs leave a trail of slime, so to be like one is to be covered in slime.

clue.text: Eggheads' turn to legislate, innit?

definitions.note: the definition is a plural noun with a possessive apostrophe, the 's acting as the link is

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist given to the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone says, in slang, that it is now the clever people's chance to make the laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innit' is British slang for 'isn't it'; the fodder is LEGISLATE plus INNIT, with 'to' only joining.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the intellectual class, the people mockingly called eggheads.

clue.text: Worried Cameron pined for mastery

indicators.note: worried means troubled and agitated, signalling the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: David Cameron is pictured fretting and longing for dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Predominance is the state of being dominant or in control, a synonym for mastery.

clue.text: Design copied on to new club?

definitions.meaning: a decal or picture moved onto a surface from a backing sheet
a footballer's move from one club to another

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a picture copied onto a surface and a player's move to a new football club.

clue.text: Light gets in through appeal to God

indicators.note: gets in means the light goes inside the word for through

parts.note: per means through or by means of
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A beam of light enters while someone makes a plea to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is a request or address made to God.

clue.text: Love poetry during which the French president starts to take fifty winks?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

indicators.note: during which places the French article inside the word for poetry

parts.note: verse is poetry
le is French for the

indicators.note: starts takes only the first letter of the word president

explanation.surface: A romantic poem is read while France's president nods off for a little longer than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forty winks' is a short nap, so fifty winks means sleeping past the time intended.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking more than forty winks means sleeping past the intended time, which is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Topsy-turvy move of season fixed around Taunton, say

parts.note: summer is a season
set means fixed or firm

explanation.surface: A seasonal acrobatic tumble is arranged in the county surrounding Taunton.
explanation.walkthrough: Summerset is an old word for somersault. 'Around Taunton, say' adds a hint that it sounds like Somerset, the English county whose county town is Taunton.
explanation.definitionFit: An old spelling of somersault, a head-over-heels flip that turns the body topsy-turvy.

clue.text: Stage show including animal — or seeking to appease

indicators.note: including means the stage show holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a play is a stage show
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A theatre production featuring an animal, or else an attempt to soothe someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Placatory describes something meant to pacify or appease.

clue.text: Father Joseph O'Donoghue's vestment

indicators.note: the possessive says the vestment belongs within the priest's name

explanation.surface: An Irish priest is described wearing his robe.
explanation.walkthrough: An ephod is the linen garment worn by priests in the Old Testament; 'Father' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod was a sleeveless priestly garment, a kind of vestment.

clue.text: Pious exclamation of Spooner as he waters magic plant?

indicators.note: naming Dr Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: moly is the magic herb Hermes gives Odysseus in Homer
hoses means waters with a hose

explanation.surface: Dr Spooner is imagined exclaiming piously while watering an enchanted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild oath, invoking the biblical lawgiver, is an exclamation of surprise with a pious flavour.

clue.text: Poem dubious for Roman theatre?

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
um is the sound of a doubtful, hesitant speaker

explanation.surface: A questionable poem is meant for a classical playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum was a roofed building in ancient Rome for music and poetry, a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Complete success should rattle the doorposts

definitions.meaning: winning every major event or every trick in a contest
read literally, an almighty slam of a door

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a total victory and, taken literally, a huge door slam.

clue.text: Young male crab?

definitions.meaning: a small boy, in British slang
a creature that nips with its pincers

explanation.definitionFit: Nipper means a small boy, and literally a creature that nips, like a crab.

clue.text: Timeless 1 across embraces ecstasy in religious picture

indicators.note: embraces puts the shortened bread round the drug letter
timeless removes one T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: the bread solved at 1 across
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A bread loaf holds a drug inside a sacred painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one T, as 'Timeless' says, leaves PITA, which then holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a religious image.

clue.text: Reciprocally, an island to provide with defenders in fight, …

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island
to man a position is to staff it with defenders for a battle

explanation.surface: An island is to be supplied with soldiers for a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: This begins the linked run of 'X to X' phrases continued by the ellipses.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-to-man describes dealings directly between two individuals, one to one in each direction.

clue.text: Contemptible chap gets most of the port

indicators.note: most of drops the opening pair of letters, leaving the larger part

parts.note: Antwerp is the great Belgian port

explanation.surface: A despicable man takes the bulk of a harbour's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or contemptible person.

clue.text: Eat up, girl!

indicators.note: up turns the word for eat upside down in a down clue

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A mother tells her daughter to finish her food.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, and crosswords commonly define any such name simply as a girl.

clue.text: … issue for drinkers in Argentinian call …

indicators.note: in places the issue and drinkers inside the Argentine's name

parts.note: Juan Peron was the Argentine president
a son is issue, meaning offspring
topers are heavy drinkers

explanation.surface: A matter for boozers comes up in a phone call from Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: A person-to-person call was one booked through an operator to a named individual; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person-to-person call is a telephone call put through to one named person only.

clue.text: … and most of beach for racing a Robin, in the short term

indicators.note: most of trims the end of the Florida name, keeping the bulk

parts.note: Daytona Beach in Florida is famous for motor racing
Sir Robin Day was a famous British television interviewer

explanation.surface: A Robin heads for most of a racing beach, but only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' merely joins; Robin is not the bird but the broadcaster Robin Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-to-day means concerned with the immediate present rather than the long run, so in the short term.

clue.text: Artificial connection between teeth and scissors

definitions.meaning: fake jewellery made of glass is called this
the word that joins tooth- and scissors-and- in two familiar phrases

explanation.definitionFit: The word means imitation gemstones and links toothpaste with scissors-and-paste.
